data_fields.name: zone polygon vertices per team count and ally team
data_fields.donor_constant: authored on a 200-unit grid, scaled by map size / 200

data_fields.name: spawn inset (edge margin)
data_fields.donor_constant: caller supplied: scav spread at call 1138, 0 at call 1470

data_fields.name: layout pick rule
data_fields.donor_constant: override if it has at least one box per team; else exact team count; else nearest larger; else nearest smaller

data_fields.name: candidate draws per call
data_fields.donor_constant: DEFAULT_TRIES = 100; every call site found passes 1

data_fields.name: scav outer attempt loop
data_fields.donor_constant: 100, ended by the first nil draw

best_idea: Store each zone as data keyed by team count, pick the nearest layout when the exact count is missing, and test a spawn point with a point-in-polygon check plus four offset points so it keeps clear of the edge.
decision_why: Zone polygons per population size belong in zone data and the pick rule and inset test belong in the engine, which is the zones-as-data shape we want. Do not copy the map-geometry fallback, the nil-then-break draw loop, or math.random for server-verified spawns.
acceptance: A server test with a zone authored for 4 teams shows a 3-team instance uses the 4-team layout; 10,000 seeded spawn draws in an L-shaped zone with inset 1 all pass containment and the four-offset check; a zone with no layout for its team count fails the test rather than falling back.
